full_judgment:
3. Prior to the institution of this suit one Shashi Kumar Sarker filed Partition Suit No. 163 of 1976 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla against the appellant, the respondent and others for partition of properties including the suit premises. The respondent appeared in that suit, filed written statement and moved an application for stay of the further proceedings of the suit till disposal of the Partition Suit No. 163 of 1976 which was rejected by the learned Munsif by order dated 29-3-79. The respondent thereafter without moving against the aforesaid order dated 29-3-79 moved the learned District Judge, Comilla under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure in T.P. Case No. 306 of 1979 praying for transfer and analogous hearing of the aforesaid title suit with the partition suit. The learned District Judge, Comilla by his order dated 29-6-81 rejected the prayer. The respondent thereafter moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1566 of 1981 and the learned Single Judge, who heard the matter, by his judgment and order dated 28-5-81 stayed further proceedings of the ejectment suit till disposal of the partition suit. Against that judgment this appeal has been preferred. 

 4. Mr. B.B. Roy Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, has urged that having regard to the facts that the matter in issue in Title Suit No. 79 of 1978 for ejectment and the Title Suit. No. 163 of 1976 are not the same and the decision of the Title Suit is not dependent on the Partition Suit and the parties are not the same the learned Single Judge has committed an error of law in staying further proceedings of Title Suit No. 76 of 1978 for ejectment and the Title Suit No. 163 of 1976. He also submits that there was no prayer for stay of further proceedings of the title suit before the High Court Division. 

 5. It appears that a petition for stay filed by the defendant was refused by the trial court on 29.3.79 against which the defendant did not file any appeal. The present appeal arises out of an application under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for the transfer of Title Suit No. 79 of 1978 pending in the 3rd Court of Munsif Comilla for trial with Partition Suit No. 163 of 1976 of the latter court as the suit properties of the Title Suit are also included in the hotch-pot of the partition suit and that the title suit is among the defendants of the partition suit which has been filed by Kumud Behari Sarker against the respondent as sole defendant for eviction from the suit property on the ground of bonafide requirement and default. In the Partition Suit No. 163 of 1976 filed by one Shashi Kumar Das he has impleaded as many as 74 persons as defendants wherein the plaintiff and the defendant of this ejectment suit are also defendants in that partition suit and the properties of the partition suit comprises 20 schedules of which schedule No. 13 embraces the suit property of the ejectment suit. The learned District Judge on consideration of the facts and circumstances was of the view that the partition suit will naturally drag on for years and as such, it is not desirable to tag on the ejectment suit to the partition suit. 

 6. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division concurred with the finding of the learned District Judge that the parties in partition suit and the title suit are not exactly the same nor the subject matter of two suits is exactly the same, nor the relief claimed in both the suits are similar nor they are pending before the same court and was of the view that both the Courts below rightly rejected the prayer for analogous hearing of two suits before the same court and there is no error of law on that count. In that view of the matter the learned Single Judge was not justified in staying the ejectment suit till disposal of the partition suit keeping it pending indefinitely till the decision of partition stilt No. 163 of 1976. The learned Single Judge having rejected the respondent's prayer for analogous trial of both the suits should not have stayed further proceedings of the Title Suit No. 79 of 1978 or ejectment till disposal of the partition Suit No. 163 of 1976.
